data.cultural_impact: The name Simeon has been popular throughout history, particularly in Europe. In France alone, it was in the top 100 names from the 16th to the 19th centuries. It is also the name of several saints and notable figures.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the old man Simeon is considered a prophet and a just and devout man who was waiting for the coming of the Messiah. When he held the baby Jesus in his arms, he recognized Him as the long-awaited Savior. This event is commemorated in the feast day of the Presentation of the Lord (February 2). Simeon's faith and anticipation remind us of the importance of seeking and recognizing God in our lives.

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament, Simeon is a righteous and devout man who is the first to recognize Jesus as the Messiah.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Simeon remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Michael Simeon in London, United Kingdom credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Simeon, which means "Obtained by God". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Simeon, deriving from the Hebrew name Shim'on, means "hearing" or "obedient." In Christian tradition, Simeon is the righteous elder who, guided by the Holy Spirit, recognizes and reverences the infant Jesus as the long-awaited Messiah.

seo.meta_description: Explore the meaning and religious significance of the name Simeon in Christianity. Discover its origin and cultural usage.
seo.description_paragraph: Simeon is a name with deep roots in the Hebrew language and Christian tradition. Derived from the Hebrew name Shim'on, meaning 'God has heard,' Simeon has been an important name throughout history. In the Bible, Simeon is the name of two significant figures: one of the twelve tribes of Israel and the old man who recognized Jesus as the Messiah. The name Simeon is still popular today, appealing to those who value history, tradition, and spirituality.
